newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Solidere up ahead of GDR issue.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Solidere up ahead of GDR issue.

text.p: Solidere shares rose on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) in the week ended on Thursday and dealers said blocs of demand orders stabilised prices ahead of the company's $125 million GDR issue expected next week.
Financial markets will close on Friday for an Independence Day holiday.
A shares rose to $114.75 from last Friday's $113.875 and B shares closed at $117.625, up from $116.375.
Turnover was 45,354 shares from last week's 45,934 and value was $5,206,291.875 from $5,259,247.7915.

"We are getting close to November 26, the date of the GDR issue. The level of prices has been maintained through considerable blocs of demand orders placed on relatively high prices throughout the week," one dealer told Reuters.
Market sources have said that Solidere will issue next Tuesday 10 million Global Depository Receipts (GDR) worth up to $125 million. Each GDR will be worth one tenth of the company's shares.
Also traded on the BSE during the week were 400 shares of piping maker Eternit. The shares rose during the week to reach $1.8125 on Thursday from $1.625 on Monday.
There was no trade in the three other listed companies: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index rose 1.89 percent on the week to 83.53 and the BLOM stock index also rose 0.86 percent to 982.45.
